label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Probability, Conditional Probability & Two-Way Tables)
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (الاحتمال, Conditional الاحتمال & Two-Way Tables)

body.en:
Why Conditional Probability Restricts the Sample Space to a Single Row or Column: In a two-way frequency table of \(N\) total individuals, let \(n(B)\) be the marginal total of individuals satisfying condition \(B\), and \(n(A \text{ and } B)\) be the interior cell count satisfying both \(A\) and \(B\). Since \(P(B) = \frac{n(B)}{N}\) and \(P(A \text{ and } B) = \frac{n(A \text{ and } B)}{N}\), the grand total \(N\) cancels directly in the conditional ratio:

\[ P(A \mid B) = \frac{P(A \text{ and } B)}{P(B)} = \frac{n(A \text{ and } B) / N}{n(B) / N} = \frac{n(A \text{ and } B)}{n(B)} \]

Thus, whenever a Digital SAT question states "If one of the [Group B] is selected at random, what is the probability that they are in [Group A]?", you simply divide the interior intersection cell \(n(A \text{ and } B)\) by the marginal total \(n(B)\) of that specific row or column.
body.ar:
Why Conditional الاحتمال Restricts the Sample Space to a Single Row or Column: In a two-way frequency الجدول of \(N\) total individuals, let \(n(B)\) be the marginal total of individuals satisfying condition \(B\), and \(n(A \text{ and } B)\) be the interior cell count satisfying both \(A\) and \(B\). Since \(P(B) = \frac{n(B)}{N}\) and \(P(A \text{ and } B) = \frac{n(A \text{ and } B)}{N}\), the grand total \(N\) cancels directly in the conditional ratio:

\[ P(A \mid B) = \frac{P(A \text{ and } B)}{P(B)} = \frac{n(A \text{ and } B) / N}{n(B) / N} = \frac{n(A \text{ and } B)}{n(B)} \]

Thus, whenever a Digital SAT question states "If one of the [Group B] is selected at random, what is the الاحتمال that they are in [Group A]?", you simply divide the interior التقاطع cell \(n(A \text{ and } B)\) by the marginal total \(n(B)\) of that specific row or column.

body.en:
Using the survey table of 200 students (80 Grade 11, 120 Grade 12; 80 prefer online, 120 prefer in-person):

What is the probability that a randomly chosen student prefers online instruction?

\[ P(\text{Online}) = \frac{\text{Total preferring online}}{\text{Grand total}} = \frac{80}{200} = 0.40\; (40\%). \]

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations

A bag contains 14 red marbles, 18 blue marbles, and 8 green marbles. If one marble is drawn at random, what is the probability that the marble is NOT green?
question.ar:
Level 1 · Foundations

A bag contains 14 red marbles, 18 blue marbles, and 8 green marbles. إذا كان one marble is drawn at random, what is the probability that the marble is NOT green?

solution.en:
Step 1: Find the grand total: \[ 14 + 18 + 8 = 40\text{ marbles}. \]

Step 2: Use the complement rule: \[ P(\text{not green}) = 1 - P(\text{green}) = 1 - \frac{8}{40} = 1 - 0.20 = 0.80 = \frac{4}{5}. \]
solution.ar:
Step 1: أوجد grand total: \[ 14 + 18 + 8 = 40\text{ marbles}. \]

Step 2: Use the complement rule: \[ P(\text{not green}) = 1 - P(\text{green}) = 1 - \frac{8}{40} = 1 - 0.20 = 0.80 = \frac{4}{5}. \]

hints.en: Use the complement rule: \(P(\text{not green}) = 1 - P(\text{green})\). Substitute and simplify: \(P(\text{not green}) = 1 - \frac{8}{40}\).
hints.ar: Use the complement rule: \(P(\text{not green}) = 1 - P(\text{green})\). عوّض بالقيم وبسّط العبارة: \(P(\text{not green}) = 1 - \frac{8}{40}\).

blocks.heading: Level 2 · Medium — Conditional Probability & Denominator Restrictions

body.en: Compute conditional probabilities \( P(A \mid B) \) by restricting the denominator to the row or column specified by 'given that' or 'of those who'.
body.ar: Compute conditional probabilities \( P(A \mid B) \) by restricting the denominator to the row or column specified by 'بما أن' or 'of those who'.

label.en: ⚠️ SAT Traps & Pitfalls — Conditional Probability & Tables
label.ar: ⚠️ SAT Traps & Pitfalls — Conditional الاحتمال & Tables

body.en:
• Denominator Restriction in 'Given That': The phrase 'given that the student is in Grade 11' restricts the entire sample space to the Grade 11 total row only (\(120\)). Dividing by the grand total (\(200\)) is the most common distractor on the SAT!
  • 'Of Which' / 'Of Those' Phrasing: Questions phrasing like 'What fraction of the students who passed were tutored?' restricts the denominator to the passed column total.
  • Independent vs. Mutually Exclusive: If two events with positive probabilities are mutually exclusive (cannot happen together, \(P(A \cap B) = 0\)), they can never be independent, because \(P(A \mid B) = 0 \neq P(A)\).
  • 'At Least One' Complement Rule: To find \(P(\text{at least 1})\), always compute \(1 - P(\text{none})\).
body.ar:
• Denominator Restriction in 'بما أن': The phrase 'بما أن the student is in Grade 11' restricts the entire sample space to the Grade 11 total row only (\(120\)). Dividing by the grand total (\(200\)) is the most common distractor on the SAT!
  • 'Of Which' / 'Of Those' Phrasing: Questions phrasing like 'What fraction of the students who passed were tutored?' restricts the denominator to the passed column total.
  • Independent vs. Mutually Exclusive: If two events with positive probabilities are mutually exclusive (cannot happen together, \(P(A \cap B) = 0\)), they can never be independent, because \(P(A \mid B) = 0 \neq P(A)\).
  • 'At Least One' Complement Rule: To find \(P(\text{at least 1})\), always compute \(1 - P(\text{none})\).

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

A study of 100 students recorded test results based on exam prep:

• Studied: 54 passed, 6 failed (60 total)
• Did not study: 18 passed, 22 failed (40 total)

What is the probability that a randomly chosen student passed the exam, given that the student studied?
question.ar:
Level 2 · Medium

A study of 100 students recorded test results based on exam prep:

• Studied: 54 passed, 6 failed (60 total)
• Did not study: 18 passed, 22 failed (40 total)

What is the probability that a randomly chosen student passed the exam, إذا علمت أن the student studied?

solution.en:
The condition 'given that the student studied' restricts the denominator to the 60 students who studied:

\[ P(\text{Passed} \mid \text{Studied}) = \frac{54}{60} = 0.90 = 90\%. \]
solution.ar:
The condition 'إذا علمت أن the student studied' restricts the denominator to the 60 students who studied:

\[ P(\text{Passed} \mid \text{Studied}) = \frac{54}{60} = 0.90 = 90\%. \]

body.en:
Problem: In a clinical trial of 250 patients, 160 received Medication X and 90 received a Placebo. Of those receiving Medication X, 120 reported relief. Of those receiving the Placebo, 30 reported relief. If a patient who reported relief is chosen at random, what is the probability they received Medication X?

Solution: The condition restricts to patients who experienced relief: \[ \text{Total with relief} = 120 + 30 = 150. \]\[ P(\text{Medication X} \mid \text{Relief}) = \frac{120}{150} = \frac{4}{5} = 0.80 = 80\%. \]
body.ar:

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced

Using the student prep table (Studied: 54 passed, 6 failed; Did not study: 18 passed, 22 failed; Total passed: 72 out of 100), are the events 'passed' and 'studied' independent?
question.ar:
Level 3 · Advanced

باستخدام student prep table (Studied: 54 passed, 6 failed; Did not study: 18 passed, 22 failed; Total passed: 72 out of 100), are the events 'passed' and 'studied' independent?

solution.en:
Step 1: Calculate marginal probability: \[ P(\text{Passed}) = \frac{72}{100} = 0.72. \]

Step 2: Compare with conditional probability: \[ P(\text{Passed} \mid \text{Studied}) = \frac{54}{60} = 0.90. \]

Since \( P(\text{Passed} \mid \text{Studied}) = 0.90 eq 0.72 = P(\text{Passed}) \), the events are not independent (studying is positively associated with passing).

Since \( P(\text{Passed} \mid \text{Studied}) = 0.90 eq 0.72 = P(\text{Passed}) \), the events are not independent (studying is positively associated with passing).

label.en: Level 4 (Synthesis) — Testing Independence in Two-Way Tables
label.ar: Level 4 (Synthesis) — Testing Independence in Two-Way Tables (الاحتمالات والاحتمال الشرطي والجداول المزدوجة)

body.en:
Problem: In a clinic study, 60 patients received Treatment A and 40 received Treatment B. If 45 of Treatment A recovered and \( k \) of Treatment B recovered, for what value of \( k \) is recovery independent of treatment?

Solution: Independence requires the conditional recovery rate in both groups to match: \[ \frac{45}{60} = \frac{k}{40} \implies 0.75 = \frac{k}{40} \implies k = 30. \]
body.ar:
الشرح الرياضي (الاحتمالات والاحتمال الشرطي والجداول المزدوجة):

Problem: In a clinic study, 60 patients received Treatment A and 40 received Treatment B. If 45 of Treatment A recovered and \( k \) of Treatment B recovered, for what value of \( k \) is recovery independent of treatment?

Solution: Independence requires the conditional recovery rate in both groups to match: \[ \frac{45}{60} = \frac{k}{40} \implies 0.75 = \frac{k}{40} \implies k = 30. \]

question.en:
Level 4 · Synthesis

A quality-control inspector tests 300 microchips from Factory X and 200 microchips from Factory Y. Exactly 4% of the chips from Factory X and 9% of the chips from Factory Y are defective. If one defective chip is selected at random from all the defective chips found, what is the probability that it came from Factory Y?
question.ar:
Level 4 · Synthesis

A quality-control inspector tests 300 microchips from حلّلy X and 200 microchips from حلّلy Y. Exactly 4% of the chips from حلّلy X and 9% of the chips from حلّلy Y are defective. إذا كان one defective chip is selected at random from all the defective chips found, what is the probability that it came from حلّلy Y?

solution.en:
Calculate the exact number of defective chips from each factory:

\[ \text{Defective X} = 0.04 \times 300 = 12, \quad \text{Defective Y} = 0.09 \times 200 = 18. \]

Total defective chips \( = 12 + 18 = 30 \). Therefore:

\[ P(\text{Factory Y} \mid \text{Defective}) = \frac{18}{30} = \frac{3}{5} = 0.60. \]
solution.ar:
احسب exact number of defective chips from each حلّلy:

\[ \text{Defective X} = 0.04 \times 300 = 12, \quad \text{Defective Y} = 0.09 \times 200 = 18. \]

Total defective chips \( = 12 + 18 = 30 \). Therefore:

\[ P(\text{Factory Y} \mid \text{Defective}) = \frac{18}{30} = \frac{3}{5} = 0.60. \]
